messages:
Iris: Quick alert: after the midnight rollout strict fncall validation on variant-delta started returning schema rejects. Example -> `SchemaError: response.items expected object, got []`.
Diego: Wasn't strict only meant for 1% canary?
Nora: Yeah; someone bumped sampling to 100% when toggling the flag for the batch deploy.
SRE-Bot: deploy/variant-delta applied at 00:12 (build 2026.03.12-00:11).
Iris: Impact is small but visible: ~0.12% rejects across ap-south. Problem: reject events currently lack route/model labels and we capture full payloads for each reject, which spikes logs.
Diego: Immediate plan: revert sampling -> 1% and set router fallback to legacy-model for routes tagged `prod/*`. Also change tracer to sampled capture (1/500) with 64KB cap.
Nora: I'll own telemetry: add labels (route_id, model_variant, strict=true) and emit `fncall.rejects.v2` and `fncall.coerce.v2`. Also enable example sampler at 1/1000 with PII scrubber.
Observability-Team: Scrubber rules recommended: redact emails, credit-card patterns, and drop any keys matching /ssn|dob/i. We'll keep hashed session_id.
Iris: Diego, can you push the routing PR? I'll approve quickly. Nora, after metrics are live we enable strict at 1% for an internal-only variant for 1 hour to collect deterministic fails.
Diego: PR -> "fix/variant-delta-sampling-fallback" created. Comment: revert strict sampling; add legacy fallback and tag fallback_used=true.
SRE-Bot: incident logged INC-2026-077 P2 assigned to Iris, Diego, Nora.
Nora: Dashboards ETA 45m: panel for reject_rate by route, coerced_count, and small example stream.
Iris: Monitoring thresholds: if prod reject_rate > 0.5% escalate to P1. Keep this thread updated.
Diego: Rollback merged; sampling back to 1%. Early checks: rejects dropped to 0.01%, fallback_used metric at 0.11%.
Nora: Example captured and filed TASK-911 for model adapter fix. I'll add a rollout checklist item to prevent sampling misedits.
Iris: Thanks all. Postmortem owners: Iris (timeline), Nora (telemetry), Diego (router). Closing for now.
